teaser: Git won as a standard, not a server. sgit is one too: every name computed from the key, a file four GETs away, any storage can serve it.
core_idea: Like git, sgit is a format rather than a product: encrypted blobs, trees, commits and refs laid out by a convention, immutable objects named by the hash of their ciphertext and marked -imm-, every name derived from the key so a file is four GETs from any host, writes one batch and a compare-and-swap, two implementations that agree; deployment is choosing where the objects live and speed is how close they are; a cache layer computed by the writer replaces server-side derived data; and the design is what remains when the server cannot read.

quotes.text: There is a server, and it is the least interesting part.
"How fast is sgit" is the wrong question. The right one is where the storage is, and how close.
Every feature had to be expressible as objects a writer produces and a reader derives.
